result:
Admins can now rename their team from a new Team section on the profile page. I haven't run tests, lint or the app, as you asked, and I didn't add a test, so this is untested.

- **Mock API:** `PATCH /teams/:teamId` in `src/testing/mocks/handlers/teams.ts` takes `{ name }`. It returns 401 if you're not signed in, 403 if you're not an admin of that team, and 400 for an empty name. Otherwise it saves the trimmed name to the mock database and returns the team.
- **Extra endpoint:** I also added `GET /teams/:teamId` to the mock, which you didn't ask for. Showing the team name needs it, because the existing `GET /teams` returns every team and would show members other teams' data. It returns 404 for any team other than the user's own. The platform team will need to build this one too.
- **API files:** `features/teams/api/update-team.ts` has the Zod schema, the fetcher and `useUpdateTeam`. `features/teams/api/get-team.ts` has the matching query hook.
- **Success message:** The "Team Renamed" toast is raised inside `useUpdateTeam`, not in the component, following `src/features/CLAUDE.md`. The existing profile, discussion and user components still raise their toasts in the component.
- **UI:** `features/teams/components/team-section.tsx` shows the team name. It shows the Rename button only to admins, using `<Authorization>`. `rename-team.tsx` is the form drawer, built from `Form`, `FormDrawer` and `Input`.
- **Profile route:** `app/routes/app/profile.tsx` renders the new section below User Information. The route is where the teams feature gets composed in, since features can't import each other.

The mock database in `localStorage` (`msw-db`) already has the team model, so no clearing should be needed.
